findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the site_settings table has no 'embed_category' row, because execute(...)[0] is nil. Discourse only persists a site setting row when it deviates from the default, so nearly every fresh install and most existing sites have no 'embed_category' row; `db:migrate` raises NoMethodError on nil for ['id'] and the deploy cannot complete.

[BUG] The migration inserts legacy embeddable_hosts values verbatim, bypassing the model's before_validation normalization that strips protocols and paths. Any site whose old embeddable_hosts setting contained entries like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234' gets rows stored with the protocol/path intact; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's `lower(host) = ?` comparison then never matches, so embedding silently stops working for all migrated hosts.

[BUG] The INSERT statement interpolates the host value directly into SQL with single quotes, so any host containing an apostrophe breaks the migration. A legacy embeddable_hosts entry containing a quote (user-typed text) produces invalid SQL and aborts db:migrate mid-way, after the table was created but before the settings cleanup runs.

[BUG] update and destroy call save_host(host)/host.destroy on a record looked up with .first, which is nil for a nonexistent or already-deleted id. A double-submit of the delete button, or a save against a host deleted in another tab, sends params[:id] with no matching row; nil.host = raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404/4xx.

[ADVISORY] The update action re-renders the fetched embedding without applying any params, making it a no-op, and no template ever wires a save button to the controller's saveChanges action. The PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and the controller's saveChanges action are dead code; an admin visiting the page has no way to persist anything other than individual host rows, and any future settings added to this screen will silently not save.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricators were moved into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb while the embeddable_host fabricator itself now lives in category_fabricator.rb — the two files' names and contents are swapped. The next contributor adding a category or embeddable-host fabricator edits the wrong file, and grep-by-filename fails; pure change-safety cost with no functional benefit to the swap.

[ADVISORY] The plural _ids hydration path calls self.pluralize(subType), which for an irregular or unchanged plural (e.g. category_ids → 'categorys' if the pluralizer lacks the y→ies rule, or a subtype whose plural differs from the payload's side-load key) produces a key the serializer never sends. Any REST-serialized model emitting foo_ids where pluralize('foo') differs from the actual side-load collection name silently gets an empty/undefined relationship; only 'colors' is exercised by the tests, so the assumption is unverified for other subtypes.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any database where the embed_category site_setting row does not exist, because `execute(...)[0]['id']` dereferences nil when the SELECT returns zero rows. On a fresh install (site_settings defaults live in site_settings.yml, not the DB) or any site that never changed embed_category, `execute(...)[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting db:migrate and blocking every subsequent deploy.

[BUG] update and destroy crash with NoMethodError when no EmbeddableHost exists for params[:id], because `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil and is passed unchecked to save_host / .destroy. A stale row in the admin UI (host already deleted in another tab) or a forged ID yields an unhandled NoMethodError and a 500 instead of a 404; save_host also does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` which raises ActionController::Parameters missing-key errors for malformed payloads.

[BUG] The migration interpolates raw host strings into SQL (`INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`), so any host value containing a single quote raises a SQL syntax error and aborts the migration. Any site whose embeddable_hosts setting contains a quote or backslash (host_list values are user-entered free text) hits ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid mid-migration; the site_settings rows are also only deleted after this point, so the site is left with a half-run migration and no data loss recovery path.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update is a silent no-op: it fetches the embedding and re-renders it without reading or persisting any params, while the client's saveChanges calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`. The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint and its route, controller action, and client wiring are shipped inert — any future embedding-level settings edited on this page are silently discarded with a 200 success response, which will bite the first developer who adds a field to the embedding serializer/template.

[ADVISORY] No JavaScript test exists for the embeddable-host component, the admin-embedding route/controller, or the `_hydrateEmbedded` plural-ids path as exercised by the new embedding adapter (pathFor override, embeddable_hosts hydration). The new frontend state machine (edit/cancel/save with buffered properties, categoryId caching) and the custom adapter pathFor override are regressible with no coverage; the store-test changes cover fruits only, so the admin embedding UI breaking would pass CI.

[ADVISORY] The diff replaces the entire contents of spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb with the embeddable_host fabricator, moving the category fabricators to spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the category fabricator now lives in a file named after an unrelated model. The next developer adding a category fabricator edits the file whose name matches (category_fabricator.rb), finds the embeddable_host fabricator there, and either duplicates or clobbers definitions; this is an unexplained file-swap that future readers will have to reverse-engineer from git history.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where no 'embed_category' row exists in site_settings, because execute(...)[0] is nil and nil['id'] is called. Every standard install (site_settings rows only exist when a value has been changed from default, so embed_category has no row) fails to run the migration, halting the deploy; the required data migration this PR exists to perform never completes.

[BUG] Migrated host values are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT statement ('#{h}') with no quoting, so any host string containing a single quote raises a SQL error mid-migration. Admins whose existing embeddable_hosts setting contains a URL with a quote character get a failed, partially-applied migration; the site_settings rows are deleted only after the inserts succeed, but a half-inserted table plus a crashed migration leaves the site unupgradable.

[BUG] expandable_first_post? silently drops the SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? guard, so the check no longer reflects the configured-embedding state at all. On a forum that has a stray TopicEmbed but no allowed hosts configured, posts are now truncated with the 'expand' UI even though embedding is effectively disabled — a behavior change not traceable to 'edit category/host relationships'.

[BUG] EmbeddingController#update accepts the PUT but saves nothing — it re-renders the fetched OpenStruct without applying any params — while the client wires a saveChanges action and the route registers a put endpoint, so the entire update path is inert scaffolding. The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint and the client's update({}) call are dead code shipped to production; any future consumer (or an admin pressing whatever UI eventually calls saveChanges) gets a silent no-op success instead of persistence.

[BUG] update passes a nil host to save_host when no record matches params[:id], causing nil.host = params[...][:host] to raise NoMethodError instead of a 404. A stale row (deleted in another tab) or hand-crafted PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a bad id returns a 500 with a backtrace instead of the 404 the REST contract implies.

[ADVISORY] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil host when the id doesn't match, raising NoMethodError. Same stale-id scenario as update: admin UI that hasn't refreshed gets a 500 on the delete button click instead of a clean 404.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricator file was gutted and repurposed to hold the embeddable_host fabricator, while the original category fabricators were moved wholesale into the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the two files' contents are swapped relative to their names. The next contributor adding a category fabricator edits the file whose name says category and finds only the host fabricator, or vice versa; this misplacement makes every future fabricator change in this area harder and hides the diff review (the fabricator swap was smuggled inside an unrelated move).

[ADVISORY] The `hydrated || []` fallback is dead code — Array#map never returns a falsy value — so the plural-hydration branch can never take its fallback, and the deletion of obj[k] now happens unconditionally even when every lookup failed, leaving an array of undefined/null entries in obj[pluralize(subType)]. A consumer hydrating *_ids whose referenced records are absent from the payload gets an attribute containing nulls instead of the attribute being left alone, and the misleading `|| []` hides that from the next maintainer debugging hydration.

[BUG] The migration copies old embeddable_hosts setting values verbatim into the host column without stripping scheme/path, while EmbeddableHost#before_validation strips them, so migrated rows with 'http://discourse.org' never match the new lookup. record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) which compares 'http://discourse.org' (stored) against 'discourse.org' (URI#host) — every embed request from a site whose old setting used the scheme-prefixed form (explicitly supported by the removed allows_embeddable_host?, which stripped the prefix) is rejected with InvalidAccess, breaking embedding for upgraded installs while the UI shows the host as configured.

[BUG] update and destroy call host.destroy / save_host(host) on the result of a where().first lookup with no nil guard, so a missing or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError on nil. A PUT/DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (double-delete from two admin tabs, or a race between the client list and a deleted row) returns a 500 instead of a 4xx; the same unguarded pattern applies to update (line 11) where nil.host= raises.

[BUG] before_validation calls self.host.sub! on a nil host before any nil check, so any request with a missing/blank embeddable_host[host] param crashes instead of returning a validation error. An API call to create with host omitted (params[:embeddable_host][:host] is nil) hits nil.sub! and returns a 500; the format validation that would produce a 4xx never runs because the callback runs first.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a no-op: update renders the serializer but never applies any params, yet the admin UI's saveChanges button calls this.get('embedding').update({}). The save action advertised in the admin embedding screen silently discards whatever future embedding-level settings are added to this screen — the button gives success feedback while persisting nothing; operators get bitten the first time a setting is added here and appears saved but isn't.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no unique index on host (or lower(host)) and no FK/index on category_id, while record_for_host does where("lower(host) = ?", host).first. Two admins can create the same host twice; record_for_host then returns an arbitrary first match, so embeds route to whichever duplicate row .first happens to return, and the non-sargable lower(host) predicate scans the table on every embed request. Admins get bitten when the two duplicates carry different categories and the effective category silently flips after any row reordering.

[ADVISORY] save_host assigns host.category_id directly from params with no validation that the category exists, so a stale categoryId from the client (deleted category) is persisted as an orphaned FK. An admin who leaves the embedding screen open while the chosen category is deleted saves a host pointing at a nonexistent category; TopicEmbed.import then creates topics with a category_id that has no row, producing broken topics with no visible error on the embedding screen.

[ADVISORY] The new plural _ids hydration branch maps over obj[k] unconditionally and assigns `hydrated || []`, so a *_ids key that is not an array (or whose sub-type is unknown, yielding an array of undefined) is silently published as a broken array rather than left alone. Any existing or future serializer emitting a scalar column matching /_ids$/ (e.g. a JSON column named tag_ids holding an object) is silently coerced through .map and either crashes hydration or replaces the value with undefined entries; the singular branch preserved the old only-if-hydrated guard, the plural branch drops it.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where the embed_category site setting was never set, because the SELECT returns no rows and `[0]['id']` is called on nil. Every existing Discourse install that never configured embed_category (the vast majority, since the default was '') fails during db:migrate, blocking upgrades entirely — the migration never reaches the DELETE and leaves the schema half-applied.

[BUG] Host values from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into a single-quoted SQL INSERT with no escaping, so any value containing a quote or backslash breaks the statement. An admin who saved a host value with an apostrophe (the old setting accepted free text, type host_list) gets an ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid during migration, halting the upgrade after the table is created but before settings are removed.

[BUG] update calls save_host on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, which is nil when the record was already deleted (or stale id from the UI), and save_host then calls nil.host=. An admin editing a host row that another admin just deleted gets a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404/422, and destroy at line 16-18 similarly crashes with NoMethodError on nil.destroy.

[BUG] The update action ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes the unchanged @embedding, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a silent no-op while the client controller's saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) implies changes are persisted. Any admin who triggers saveChanges believes embedding settings were saved, but nothing is written; the API returns success_json-shaped output for a write that never happened — a silent data-loss contract violation.

[ADVISORY] Replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with eh.try(:category_id) changes feed-polling/import behavior: when the embed URL's host has no EmbeddableHost record, category becomes nil and topics land in Uncategorized with no operator control. Sites using feed polling (feed_polling_url) with hosts not listed in the new embeddable_hosts table get all imported topics dumped into Uncategorized after upgrade — the old embed_category setting is deleted by the migration, so the previous per-site choice is silently discarded for this path.

[ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside change (not up), and the raw INSERT data is never reversible, so a rollback permanently destroys the original configuration with no way to reconstruct it. An operator who rolls back this release loses the entire allow-list configuration irrecoverably; the destructive DELETE should be in an irreversible up with a documented backup path.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricator file was gutted and repurposed to define Fabricator(:embeddable_host) with the real category fabricators moved to a new file, leaving a file whose name no longer matches any fabricator it defines. The next contributor editing category fabricators follows the filename to spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb, finds no :category definition there, and either duplicates the fabricators or edits the wrong file — a change-safety trap created purely by file naming.

[BUG] update and destroy call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without checking the record exists, so save_host(nil)/nil.destroy raise NoMethodError when the id is unknown or stale. An admin editing the embedding page after a host was deleted in another session (or passing any bad id) gets a 500 instead of a 404/422; the destroy action crashes before render_json_error has any chance to produce a contract-compliant response.

[ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update does not mutate @embedding at all — it just re-serializes the object fetched by fetch_embedding, ignoring the PUT payload entirely. The admin UI's 'save changes' button (admin-embedding.js saveChanges → embedding.update({})) silently succeeds while persisting nothing, so operators believe embedding settings were saved when they were not.

[ADVISORY] record_for_host compares lower(stored_host) against the incoming URI host without downcasing the incoming side, and URI#host preserves case, so a Referer whose host is non-lowercase (e.g. from a crafted fetch, some proxies, or an admin who stored a mixed-case host) fails to match. Allowed hosts stored with uppercase letters are unreachable for embed authorization (only the stored side is normalized), producing intermittent deny behavior on the embed/comments path; a referer-handling middleware or non-lowercasing client silently breaks embedding.

[ADVISORY] The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is a single assertion that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController, which is a class-graph check that passes no matter what the controller's request handling does. None of the new CRUD behavior is exercised: create/update payload parsing (params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises ActionController::ParameterMissing when the key is absent, producing a 500 instead of a 4xx), the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, validation-failure render_json_error, and destroy on a nonexistent id (host.destroy on nil raises NoMethodError → 500) all ship with zero verification; a regression in any of them passes CI.

[ADVISORY] The Admin::EmbeddingController spec asserts only subclass inheritance and never issues a request, so the show/update serialization of the OpenStruct-backed embedding (including the embeddable_hosts has_many embed: :ids payload) is completely unverified. The frontend route's entire data contract — GET /admin/customize/embedding returning root 'embedding' with embeddable_host_ids plus side-loaded hosts — has no spec; a serializer change or typo in fetch_embedding ships green and the admin page breaks at runtime with no test failure.

[ADVISORY] The 'find embedded' test requests store.find('fruit', 2) but the pretender handler for '/fruits/:id' unconditionally returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]), so the assertions on colors length 2 and ids [1,2] verify apple's fixture, not the record the test asked for — the test passes even if per-id lookup hydration of the requested record is broken. The plural-hydration path (_hydrateEmbedded's new _ids branch) is only genuinely covered by findAll; any defect specific to single-record find with color_ids (e.g. hydration keyed off the wrong record) is masked because the test data and the returned fixture disagree, and a future reader of the test is misled into thinking fruit 2's color_ids [3] was the input.

[ADVISORY] The new plural-hydration branch `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` silently falls back to an empty array whenever _lookupSubType misses, and the only tests added cover the happy path where every referenced id resolves — no test exercises a color_ids entry with no matching side-loaded record. The 'empty but valid' vs 'missing' sentinel distinction is untested: when the server omits a referenced record (e.g. an embeddable host pointing at a deleted category_id), the store fabricates an empty list and the admin UI renders zero rows with no error, and no spec would catch a regression or a fix in that branch. Test files checked for coverage of this: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 (only happy-path find/findAll assertions on ids 1–3 all present).

[BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site_setting row is absent or has no matching category, which is the default state for nearly every install. Discourse only writes a site_settings row when an admin has set the setting; on any site that never set embed_category the SELECT returns zero rows, `embeddable_hosts[0]` is nil, and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration mid-deploy so the new code (which reads EmbeddableHost exclusively) has no table at all.

[BUG] The data migration guards the row inserts on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`, which is always 0 for a SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the inserts never run while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old settings. Every site's configured embeddable_hosts list is deleted from site_settings with zero rows written to embeddable_hosts; embedding breaks for all previously-configured forums and the data is unrecoverable (no backup/export step before the DELETE).

[BUG] Host values from the old setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL without parameterization or the model's normalization (which strips scheme and path). A host line containing an apostrophe breaks the SQL statement and aborts the migration; hosts stored with 'http://' prefixes or trailing paths (which the old setting allowed and the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? handled by parsing) are copied verbatim, so old rows are silently misinterpreted relative to the new EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? semantics.

[ADVISORY] create_table uses force: true on a migration that also performs destructive data operations. If the migration is ever re-run (or run against an environment where embeddable_hosts already exists, e.g. restored from a partial run), force: true silently drops the table including any hosts admins created since, then re-inserts from the now-deleted settings source.

[ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside a `change` block with no down path, making the migration irreversible. `rake db:rollback` raises IrreversibleMigration and the deleted setting values cannot be reconstructed; an operator who needs to roll back this deploy to the previous code version finds that code still reads SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, which is now gone, so rollback requires manual data resurrection.

[ADVISORY] The category backfill joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but Discourse category-type settings store 'name,slug' pairs and category names are not unique across sites with renamed categories, so the target category resolution is lossy. Sites where embed_category was stored in the 'name,slug' form get no join match and silently fall back to uncategorized, re-classifying every migrated host's posting category without any warning.

[BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record when the id doesn't exist. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id raises NoMethodError (undefined method `destroy' for nil), returning a raw 500 instead of a 404 the admin API contract implies; the user sees an unhandled error page rather than a meaningful message.

[BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] and host without any presence checks, so a missing id (update) or a missing/blank embeddable_host param raises instead of rendering a 4xx. PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:bad_id raises NoMethodError on nil.save (500), and a POST/PUT whose payload lacks the embeddable_host envelope crashes with NoMethodError for nil[:]; before_validation's host.sub! also raises on a nil host param. All three are raw 500s where render_json_error/4xx belongs.

[BUG] The delete action's destroyRecord() promise chain has no .catch, unlike save which uses popupAjaxError. When the DELETE request fails (network error, 500, stale record), the rejection is silently swallowed: no error dialog appears, the row stays in the list, and the admin believes the host was deleted while it still authorizes embeds — a user-facing operation whose failure is invisible.

[ADVISORY] The update action persists nothing; it re-renders the fetched embedding as success. The frontend saveChanges() PUTs to /admin/customize/embedding and gets a 200 with serialized data, so any future payload passed to it is silently dropped while the UI reports success — a silent no-op on a mutation endpoint.

[ADVISORY] save() persists to the server but never commits or discards the buffered changes, leaving the buffer dirty after a successful save. After saving, a later edit-then-cancel on the same row calls rollbackBuffer(), which re-renders the row with the pre-save host name/category in the UI while the server holds the new values — the admin sees stale state that disagrees with what's actually enforced until a page reload.

[ADVISORY] addHost pushes a createRecord('embeddable-host') into the list with no rollback if the user navigates away or the record is never saved. The route's model is not dirtied and the unsaved row is only cleaned up by explicit cancel, so navigating away mid-edit silently discards the admin's typed host with no confirmation or warning.

If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.

An admin editing a host row that another admin just deleted gets a NoMethodError 500 instead of a 404/422, and destroy at line 16-18 similarly crashes with NoMethodError on nil.destroy.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, the record is fetched via `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally passed to `save_host(host)`. If no record exists (stale/deleted id), `host` is `nil` and `save_host` immediately calls `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...`, causing a `NoMethodError` (500) instead of a not-found response. Similarly, `#destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then `host.destroy` without a nil check, which will also raise on missing records.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The update action ignores the request body entirely and just re-serializes the unchanged @embedding, so the PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint is a silent no-op while the client controller's saveChanges action (admin-embedding.js.es6 line 6) implies changes are persisted. Any admin who triggers saveChanges believes embedding settings were saved, but nothing is written; the API returns success_json-shaped output for a write that never happened — a silent data-loss contract violation.

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores `params` and simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` (no write side effects), making `PUT /admin/customize/embedding` a no-op. The client controller has `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, which would issue that PUT and appear “successful” while persisting nothing. One detail in the finding is off: the endpoint returns the serialized `embedding`, not `success_json`-shaped output, but the core complaint (silent no-op update) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Replacing SiteSetting.embed_category with eh.try(:category_id) changes feed-polling/import behavior: when the embed URL's host has no EmbeddableHost record, category becomes nil and topics land in Uncategorized with no operator control. Sites using feed polling (feed_polling_url) with hosts not listed in the new embeddable_hosts table get all imported topics dumped into Uncategorized after upgrade — the old embed_category setting is deleted by the migration, so the previous per-site choice is silently discarded for this path.

adjudication.rationale: In the new flow, `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` now blocks retrieval/import when there is no `EmbeddableHost` record (`!EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(@embed_url)` in `lib/topic_retriever.rb`), so the described scenario “host has no record → import still happens and lands in Uncategorized” isn’t supported by the diff. Additionally, `embeddable_hosts.category_id` is `null: false` in the migration and `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` forces a blank category to `uncategorized_category_id`, so when a host *does* exist its category_id shouldn’t be nil. While `SiteSetting.embed_category` is deleted, the migration explicitly attempts to carry it forward by setting `category_id` for inserted `embeddable_hosts` rows based on the prior `embed_category` setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside change (not up), and the raw INSERT data is never reversible, so a rollback permanently destroys the original configuration with no way to reconstruct it. An operator who rolls back this release loses the entire allow-list configuration irrecoverably; the destructive DELETE should be in an irreversible up with a documented backup path.

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration is defined with `change` but performs destructive, non-reversible operations via raw SQL: it copies data out of `site_settings` and then `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no `down` path to restore those deleted settings, so if the release is rolled back the original allow-list/category configuration cannot be reconstructed from the database (and Rails cannot auto-reverse the raw `execute`/DELETE). This is a real rollback/data-loss risk grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The category fabricator file was gutted and repurposed to define Fabricator(:embeddable_host) with the real category fabricators moved to a new file, leaving a file whose name no longer matches any fabricator it defines. The next contributor editing category fabricators follows the filename to spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb, finds no :category definition there, and either duplicates the fabricators or edits the wrong file — a change-safety trap created purely by file naming.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `Fabricator(:category)`; it now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (with `host` and `category`). The `:category` (and related) fabricators were moved into the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. This filename/content mismatch is a maintainability/change-safety trap (contributors looking for category fabricators will likely edit/duplicate the wrong file), but it does not introduce a direct runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first without checking the record exists, so save_host(nil)/nil.destroy raise NoMethodError when the id is unknown or stale. An admin editing the embedding page after a host was deleted in another session (or passing any bad id) gets a 500 instead of a 404/422; the destroy action crashes before render_json_error has any chance to produce a contract-compliant response.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call methods on it (`save_host(host)` which does `host.host = ...`, and `host.destroy`). If the id is stale/unknown, `host` will be `nil` and these calls will raise `NoMethodError`, producing a 500 instead of a controlled 404/422 response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Admin::EmbeddingController#update does not mutate @embedding at all — it just re-serializes the object fetched by fetch_embedding, ignoring the PUT payload entirely. The admin UI's 'save changes' button (admin-embedding.js saveChanges → embedding.update({})) silently succeeds while persisting nothing, so operators believe embedding settings were saved when they were not.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `#update` does not apply any params/payload and simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` (same as `#show`), so the PUT endpoint is effectively a no-op. The client controller (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`) defines `saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`, which would also persist nothing if wired up. However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not include any “save changes” button or call `saveChanges`, and the only persisted changes shown in the diff are via `EmbeddableHost#save/destroyRecord`. So the finding’s “operators believe settings were saved” UI claim isn’t directly evidenced here, but the no-op update endpoint / dead action is a concrete diff-grounded issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] record_for_host compares lower(stored_host) against the incoming URI host without downcasing the incoming side, and URI#host preserves case, so a Referer whose host is non-lowercase (e.g. from a crafted fetch, some proxies, or an admin who stored a mixed-case host) fails to match. Allowed hosts stored with uppercase letters are unreachable for embed authorization (only the stored side is normalized), producing intermittent deny behavior on the embed/comments path; a referer-handling middleware or non-lowercasing client silently breaks embedding.
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same case-insensitivity bug: the query lowercases the stored host (lower(host) = ?) but does not normalize/downcase the incoming host parameter, so mixed-case Referer/URI hosts may not match as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The entire spec for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController is a single assertion that the class inherits from Admin::AdminController, which is a class-graph check that passes no matter what the controller's request handling does. None of the new CRUD behavior is exercised: create/update payload parsing (params[:embeddable_host][:host] raises ActionController::ParameterMissing when the key is absent, producing a 500 instead of a 4xx), the blank-category fallback to uncategorized_category_id, validation-failure render_json_error, and destroy on a nonexistent id (host.destroy on nil raises NoMethodError → 500) all ship with zero verification; a regression in any of them passes CI.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` CRUD actions that can raise 500s on common edge cases: `destroy` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then calls `host.destroy` without checking for nil, so a nonexistent id will trigger `NoMethodError`. Similarly, `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` / `[:category_id]` with no guard, so missing/incorrect payloads will also raise (nil `params[:embeddable_host]`). The added controller spec indeed only checks inheritance and would not catch these behaviors.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Admin::EmbeddingController spec asserts only subclass inheritance and never issues a request, so the show/update serialization of the OpenStruct-backed embedding (including the embeddable_hosts has_many embed: :ids payload) is completely unverified. The frontend route's entire data contract — GET /admin/customize/embedding returning root 'embedding' with embeddable_host_ids plus side-loaded hosts — has no spec; a serializer change or typo in fetch_embedding ships green and the admin page breaks at runtime with no test failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new Admin::EmbeddingController (show/update) that renders an OpenStruct via EmbeddingSerializer with `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids` (expecting an `embeddable_host_ids` array plus a sideloaded `embeddable_hosts` collection). However, the only new spec for this controller (`spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) merely asserts it subclasses Admin::AdminController and never performs `get :show`/`put :update` or validates the JSON payload shape/root key. Therefore the PR introduces nontrivial controller/serializer data-contract behavior without any test coverage, and a serializer/root/side-load mismatch could ship green and break the admin page at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The 'find embedded' test requests store.find('fruit', 2) but the pretender handler for '/fruits/:id' unconditionally returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]), so the assertions on colors length 2 and ids [1,2] verify apple's fixture, not the record the test asked for — the test passes even if per-id lookup hydration of the requested record is broken. The plural-hydration path (_hydrateEmbedded's new _ids branch) is only genuinely covered by findAll; any defect specific to single-record find with color_ids (e.g. hydration keyed off the wrong record) is masked because the test data and the returned fixture disagree, and a future reader of the test is misled into thinking fruit 2's color_ids [3] was the input.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the Pretender handler for `this.get('/fruits/:id'...)` always sets `const fruit = fruits[0];` and returns that, regardless of `:id`. Meanwhile `store-test.js.es6` changed the "find embedded" test to call `store.find('fruit', 2)` and assert `colors` has length 2 with ids 1 and 2—values that match `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`), not fruit id 2 (banana, `color_ids: [3]`). This means the test can pass even if per-id record lookup/hydration is incorrect, making it a real, diff-grounded test weakness rather than a production bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new plural-hydration branch `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` silently falls back to an empty array whenever _lookupSubType misses, and the only tests added cover the happy path where every referenced id resolves — no test exercises a color_ids entry with no matching side-loaded record. The 'empty but valid' vs 'missing' sentinel distinction is untested: when the server omits a referenced record (e.g. an embeddable host pointing at a deleted category_id), the store fabricates an empty list and the admin UI renders zero rows with no error, and no spec would catch a regression or a fix in that branch. Test files checked for coverage of this: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 (only happy-path find/findAll assertions on ids 1–3 all present).

adjudication.rationale: In the new plural-hydration branch in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, `const hydrated = obj[k].map(...)` will always produce a truthy array; if `_lookupSubType` can’t resolve an id, the resulting array will contain `undefined`/`null` entries, not trigger `hydrated || []` to become `[]`. So the finding’s claim that it “silently falls back to an empty array whenever _lookupSubType misses” (and that the UI would therefore show “zero rows”) is not supported by the diff. While the tests only cover the happy path for `color_ids`, the specific described fallback behavior is a misread of the implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site_setting row is absent or has no matching category, which is the default state for nearly every install. Discourse only writes a site_settings row when an admin has set the setting; on any site that never set embed_category the SELECT returns zero rows, `embeddable_hosts[0]` is nil, and `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration mid-deploy so the new code (which reads EmbeddableHost exclusively) has no table at all.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it unconditionally does `execute(... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category' )[0]['id'].to_i`. If the SELECT returns 0 rows (e.g., no `site_settings` row for `embed_category` or no matching category name), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the migration before the fallback `if category_id == 0` can run. This matches the finding and would break deploys on sites without that setting row.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The data migration guards the row inserts on `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`, which is always 0 for a SELECT in PostgreSQL, so the inserts never run while the paired DELETE unconditionally destroys the old settings. Every site's configured embeddable_hosts list is deleted from site_settings with zero rows written to embeddable_hosts; embedding breaks for all previously-configured forums and the data is unrecoverable (no backup/export step before the DELETE).

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, it does `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and then guards inserts with `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. In PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` is not the right way to check whether a SELECT returned rows (it commonly returns 0/empty for SELECT), so this condition can prevent migrating any rows even when the setting exists. Immediately after, the migration unconditionally runs `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`, which would erase the old configuration even if nothing was inserted into `embeddable_hosts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Host values from the old setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL without parameterization or the model's normalization (which strips scheme and path). A host line containing an apostrophe breaks the SQL statement and aborts the migration; hosts stored with 'http://' prefixes or trailing paths (which the old setting allowed and the removed SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? handled by parsing) are copied verbatim, so old rows are silently misinterpreted relative to the new EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? semantics.
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that host values are interpolated directly into an INSERT SQL statement without parameterization, noting that quotes can break the SQL and implying injection/unsafe SQL construction. This is the same core issue as the golden comment about string interpolation in SQL and the need for parameter binding/proper quoting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] create_table uses force: true on a migration that also performs destructive data operations. If the migration is ever re-run (or run against an environment where embeddable_hosts already exists, e.g. restored from a partial run), force: true silently drops the table including any hosts admins created since, then re-inserts from the now-deleted settings source.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which will drop and recreate the table if it already exists. The same migration also migrates data from `site_settings` and then executes `DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')`. If the migration is re-run or applied in a state where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g. partial/failed run, manual table creation), `force: true` can silently destroy any existing admin-created rows and the subsequent re-seed may be incomplete/empty because the settings source is deleted in this migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside a `change` block with no down path, making the migration irreversible. `rake db:rollback` raises IrreversibleMigration and the deleted setting values cannot be reconstructed; an operator who needs to roll back this deploy to the previous code version finds that code still reads SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts, which is now gone, so rollback requires manual data resurrection.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration is defined with `change` but runs multiple `execute` statements and ends by `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. Rails cannot automatically reverse raw SQL in a `change` migration, so `db:rollback` would be irreversible, and deleting the old site_settings rows also means the prior values can’t be recovered if you roll back to code that expects those settings. This is a real operational/rollback concern, not a forward-runtime defect in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The category backfill joins site_settings.value to categories.name, but Discourse category-type settings store 'name,slug' pairs and category names are not unique across sites with renamed categories, so the target category resolution is lossy. Sites where embed_category was stored in the 'name,slug' form get no join match and silently fall back to uncategorized, re-classifying every migrated host's posting category without any warning.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` resolves the old `embed_category` setting via `INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and then falls back to `uncategorized_category_id` when `category_id == 0`. This mapping is lossy/fragile because it depends on matching a stored setting string to `categories.name` (which can change and is not guaranteed unique), so it can mis-resolve or fail to resolve the intended category and migrate all hosts to the fallback category. This is a data-migration correctness issue introduced by the diff, even if the exact prior storage format ('name,slug') is not proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a nil record when the id doesn't exist. DELETE /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id raises NoMethodError (undefined method `destroy' for nil), returning a raw 500 instead of a 404 the admin API contract implies; the user sees an unhandled error page rather than a meaningful message.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy` (and renders success) without checking for `nil`. If the id is stale/nonexistent, `host` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError` (`undefined method 'destroy' for nil:NilClass`), producing a 500 rather than a controlled 404/JSON error. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] and host without any presence checks, so a missing id (update) or a missing/blank embeddable_host param raises instead of rendering a 4xx. PUT /admin/embeddable_hosts/:bad_id raises NoMethodError on nil.save (500), and a POST/PUT whose payload lacks the embeddable_host envelope crashes with NoMethodError for nil[:]; before_validation's host.sub! also raises on a nil host param. All three are raw 500s where render_json_error/4xx belongs.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return `nil`, but `save_host(host)` immediately dereferences it (`host.host = ...`, `host.save`), causing a 500 (NoMethodError) instead of a 4xx/404. Similarly, `save_host` assumes `params[:embeddable_host]` exists and does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`/`[:category_id]`, which will raise if the request payload lacks the `embeddable_host` envelope. Additionally, `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` without guarding against `self.host` being nil, which can also raise during create/update when host is missing/blank.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete action's destroyRecord() promise chain has no .catch, unlike save which uses popupAjaxError. When the DELETE request fails (network error, 500, stale record), the rejection is silently swallowed: no error dialog appears, the row stays in the list, and the admin believes the host was deleted while it still authorizes embeds — a user-facing operation whose failure is invisible.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...)` but does not attach a `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()`, which uses `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE request fails, no `popupAjaxError` (or other UI feedback) will be shown from this code path, leaving the failure unhandled at the component level.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update action persists nothing; it re-renders the fetched embedding as success. The frontend saveChanges() PUTs to /admin/customize/embedding and gets a 200 with serialized data, so any future payload passed to it is silently dropped while the UI reports success — a silent no-op on a mutation endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply re-renders `@embedding` without applying or persisting any request params (it calls `render_serialized` only). The frontend controller action `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({});`, which will issue a PUT to `/admin/customize/embedding` (see `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` and routes.rb) and receive a 200/serialized response even though the server performed no mutation. This is a silent no-op on a mutation endpoint as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] save() persists to the server but never commits or discards the buffered changes, leaving the buffer dirty after a successful save. After saving, a later edit-then-cancel on the same row calls rollbackBuffer(), which re-renders the row with the pre-save host name/category in the UI while the server holds the new values — the admin sees stale state that disagrees with what's actually enforced until a page reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the component uses `bufferedProperty('host')` and calls `rollbackBuffer()` on cancel, but in the `save()` success path it never calls a corresponding `commitBuffer()`/buffer reset. Since `edit()` just toggles `editToggled` and does not recreate the buffer, the buffered-content mixin can retain its pre-save “original” snapshot; a later edit-then-cancel would roll back to that snapshot rather than the just-saved values, producing the stale UI state described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] addHost pushes a createRecord('embeddable-host') into the list with no rollback if the user navigates away or the record is never saved. The route's model is not dirtied and the unsaved row is only cleaned up by explicit cancel, so navigating away mid-edit silently discards the admin's typed host with no confirmation or warning.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addHost()` creating a new unsaved record (`this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')`) and pushing it into `embedding.embeddable_hosts` (admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6). The only cleanup path for a new row is the component’s `cancel()` action, which just calls `deleteHost` to remove it from the array and does not `destroyRecord()`/`rollbackAttributes()` (admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 + controller `deleteHost`). There is also no route-level `willTransition`/deactivate hook shown to warn or roll back unsaved edits if the admin navigates away. That said, the claim about “route’s model is not dirtied” / guaranteed data loss on navigation isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone (Ember/store caching and transition behavior aren’t shown), so this is best treated as a concrete UX/state-management concern rather than a proven functional defect.
